key_idea: Combine a system of tiling equations into one tile by attaching each F_m to a block E_m of a 'rigid' partition of Z/NZ, where every translate of one block meets every translate of another unless the shifts coincide, so any tiling is forced to be a graph over a common A that solves every equation at once.
reason: The visible core argument for Theorem 11 is short and conceptual: the rigid-partition property (7) does all the work, and the graph/vertical-line counting argument follows directly from it and is easy to follow. Still, the overall proof is a long chain of reductions (lifting, concatenation, expressibility, library-building, then a Sudoku construction with case analysis that is only summarized), so the excerpt shows tidy modular bookkeeping more than one inevitable idea.
recognized: Greenfeld–Tao, 'A counterexample to the periodic tiling conjecture' (Annals of Math. 2024)
